chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Kazzaz and Ali ibn al-Hakam from Muthanna al-Hannat from Zurara ibn A'yan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked: A woman left behind her husband, her mother, her full siblings (from both parents), her maternal siblings, and her paternal siblings. He said: 'For her husband is half, for her mother is one-sixth, and for the maternal siblings is one-third, and the paternal and maternal siblings are excluded.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: This report is not acted upon because we have clarified that with the mother, no one from the siblings (full, maternal, or paternal) inherits. It is likely that the narration came down due to precaution (taqiyyah) to coincide with the views of some of the Sunni majority.

key_terms.التَّقِيَّةُ: Precaution (in Shia jurisprudence, often used to explain discrepancies in narrations)

ai.seo_question: How is inheritance distributed when a deceased woman leaves behind a husband, mother, and multiple types of siblings?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq details the inheritance shares for a woman leaving a husband, mother, and various siblings, assigning half to the husband, one-sixth to the mother, and one-third to the maternal siblings while excluding paternal and maternal siblings. The commentator, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, notes this ruling is likely due to *taqiyyah* (precaution) to align with Sunni jurisprudence, as Shia law typically excludes all siblings when the mother is present. This highlights the nuanced interplay between explicit textual transmission and practical legal application in Shia fiqh.
